guarantees.claim: When rst_ni is low, reqid_q and reqsz_q are cleared to 0, and rspop_q is set to AccessAck.
When not in reset and a_ack is asserted, reqid_q is updated with tl_i.a_source, reqsz_q with tl_i.a_size, and rspop_q becomes AccessAckData if rd_req is true, else AccessAck.

formal.consequent: reqid_q == tl_i.a_source && reqsz_q == tl_i.a_size && rspop_q == (rd_req ? AccessAckData : AccessAck)

formal_sketch.consequent: reqid_q == tl_i.a_source && reqsz_q == tl_i.a_size && rspop_q == (rd_req ? AccessAckData : AccessAck)

guarantees.claim: When not in reset and a_ack is deasserted, reqid_q, reqsz_q and rspop_q hold their previous values.

assumptions.claim: When a_ack is asserted, tl_i.a_source and tl_i.a_size must be stable and valid.
assumptions.risk: Captured ID/size mismatch may route the response to the wrong destination or misinterprets the response size.

assumptions.claim: rd_req must correctly indicate whether the acknowledged transaction is a read when a_ack is asserted.
assumptions.risk: Incorrect rspop_q leads to wrong response opcode, causing upstream to misinterpret the response (e.g., treating a write response as data response).

formal.consequent: rd_req matches the acknowledged request type

formal_sketch.consequent: rd_req matches the acknowledged request type

assumptions.claim: a_ack must be low when rst_ni is released (transitions from low to high).
assumptions.risk: A spurious capture after reset may store stale or undefined values.

assumptions.claim: a_ack must be a single-cycle pulse.
assumptions.risk: If a_ack remains high for multiple cycles, reqid_q, reqsz_q and rspop_q update every cycle, possibly sending multiple responses for one transaction and violating protocol.

uncertain_points.claim: The block sets rspop_q to AccessAckData for all reads, irrespective of any error condition (comment 'regardless of error'). It is unclear whether errors should suppress the data response or if upstream logic guarantees data clearing/zeroization.
uncertain_points.cond: A read request is acknowledged while an internal error (e.g., permission violation) is present.
uncertain_points.risk: If an erroneous read returns valid secret data via AccessAckData, sensitive information may be leaked.

formal_sketch.antecedent: A read request is acknowledged while an internal error (e.g., permission violation) is present
formal_sketch.consequent: The block sets rspop_q to AccessAckData for all reads, irrespective of any error condition (comment 'regardless of error'). It is unclear whether errors should suppress the data response or if upstream logic guarantees data clearing/zeroiza

uncertain_points.claim: If a_ack is asserted for more than one cycle, reqid_q, reqsz_q, and rspop_q will be repeatedly updated, potentially causing multiple responses for a single transaction. The design assumes a single-cycle a_ack but contains no width enforcement.
uncertain_points.cond: a_ack remains high for N > 1 cycles
uncertain_points.risk: Protocol violation and possible data corruption or bandwidth waste.

security_implications: The chunk unconditionally sets rspop_q = AccessAckData on any read acknowledgement, ignoring error signals (comment 'regardless of error'). If an access error occurs (e.g., permission denied), the adapter still signals a data response, which could cause the initiator to accept data from a failed transaction. Unless upstream logic explicitly clears or masks the data path on errors, this behavior may leak secret/confidential data from an unauthorized access. This needs cross‑chunk verification of error handling and data zeroization.
